summary: Install-time host identifier beacon to hardcoded bare IP over plain HTTP
details: setup.py registers custom build_py and install cmdclasses that, on every `pip install` or sdist build, POST a JSON payload containing socket.gethostname(), the install path, os.getcwd(), the Python version, and a canary identifier to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://13.140.137.222:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The destination is a non-publisher bare IP, there is no opt-in, and the package name resembles an internal vendor name, so any environment whose internal dependency resolves to this public name has host and path identifiers transmitted off-host at install time. The long_description self-labels this as an 'authorized dependency-confusion canary' targeting Backblaze/Bugcrowd, but the exfiltration mechanism is identical to a hostile dependency-confusion payload and the authorization claim is author-controlled text that an installer cannot verify at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
